description: We are a team of AI developers and Web engineers combining Machine Learning with modern Web development. For the "Field Shift" challenge, we are building an intelligent, interactive decision-support web app that analyzes NASA Earth observation data to recommend optimal crop rotation strategies for local farmers. We aim to convert complex spatial data into actionable insights for sustainable agriculture
summary: FieldShift is a data-driven crop rotation advisor for Egyptian smallholder farmers. It addresses the challenge by integrating three real satellite and climate datasets — NASA POWER, MODIS NDVI, and ISRIC SoilGrids — to diagnose field conditions and recommend rotation plans based on actual observed data, not generic advice. It is important because Egyptian agriculture faces compounding pressures of heat stress, soil salinization, and water scarcity
details:
FieldShift is a client-side web application built for Arabic-speaking farmers in Egypt’s Nile Delta. It follows a four-screen flow: (1) My Field — the farmer enters location, prior crops, soil knowledge, irrigation budget, and restrictions; (2) Compare Rotations — the tool presents a baseline rotation plus two feasible alternatives on aligned seasonal timelines, with explicit infeasibility reasons before ranking; (3) Test Conditions — the farmer adjusts water budgets to see how constraints change; (4) Why This Plan? — each result exposes its data source, observation period, spatial resolution, transformations, assumptions, and limitations.

The core pipeline is fully deterministic: farmer inputs + cached NASA-derived environmental features + sourced crop rules → feasibility filtering → indicator scoring (water burden, heat exposure, cover days, soil-family diversity) → ranked rotation comparison. No ML or prediction is used. Each indicator shows whether it comes from farmer-provided data, satellite-derived data, model-estimated data, or an agronomic rule.

Tools & Languages: JavaScript/React (frontend), Python (offline data acquisition and seasonal feature processing), NASA POWER REST API, MODIS MOD13Q1 via ORNL DAAC, ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0, FAO-56 Penman-Monteith methodology for ET₀. The app supports Arabic RTL and English LTR, is mobile-friendly, and runs offline using cached demo data when remote APIs are unavailableFieldShift is a client-side web application built for Arabic-speaking farmers in Egypt’s Nile Delta.
